plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Silvery-green mounds send up slender spikes of tiny, fragrant violet-blue flowers. Their scent drifts across sun-baked hillsides and hums with bees. In the fields of Provence, the flowers stretch in long, rolling purple rows toward the horizon.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-June to late August, with peak bloom in July; late-season blooms still colour the fields on July 29
plants.funFact: Lavender's name comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'. Romans used it to scent their baths and laundry.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: South Africa's national flower is a showy, dinner-plate-sized bloom. A crown of creamy-pink bracts surrounds a downy center. It opens in the cool of the Southern Hemisphere winter, when little else in the fynbos is flowering.
plants.bloomingSeason: July to October, so the first blooms open around July 29 in the Southern Hemisphere winter
plants.location: Fynbos regions of the Western and Eastern Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: Proteas belong to an ancient plant family that dates back to the age of Gondwana. The family's name honors Proteus, the Greek sea god who could change his shape.

plants.name: Echinacea purpurea
plants.description: Daisy-like blooms with drooping rosy-purple petals surround a spiky, copper-orange central cone. In summer meadows and gardens, they are favorites of butterflies, bumblebees and goldfinches. Goldfinches also come later for the seeds.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer, roughly June through August (it may repeat in early fall); in full bloom on July 29
plants.location: Eastern and central North America, widely grown in gardens and prairies
plants.funFact: The 'cone' at the center is a dense cluster of tiny true flowers. The genus name comes from the Greek 'echinos', meaning hedgehog, for its prickly center.
